Daily Briefings · Tuesday, November 17, 2026

Space & Defense Daily — Tuesday, Nov 17, 2026

ULA's first look at Sunday's Vulcan failure points to low booster performance just after liftoff, deepening the U.S. military launch crunch; NATO launched its STARLIFT launch-access initiative and a Space Force-backed Global Data Marketplace for commercial space data; Senate appropriators unveiled a $1.1T FY27 Pentagon bill with $9.4B for Golden Dome, while European allies rushed air defences to Ukraine.

← NewerWed, Nov 18, 2026All briefingsOlder →Mon, Nov 16, 2026
NATOEuropean UnionUnited StatesEuropean spaceGlobal space & defense

Top stories: ULA says early data show Sunday's Vulcan flight suffered low booster performance right after liftoff, so the stages separated too low and too slow for orbit. That leaves SpaceX as the only certified NSSL launcher flying for now. At NATO EDGE 26 in İzmir, the Alliance launched STARLIFT, a pooled service to secure short-notice military launches funded by 10 allies plus South Korea, along with a Global Data Marketplace for commercial space data built on a Space Force platform. In Washington, Senate appropriators released a $1.1T FY27 defense bill that folds about $69B of the White House's reconciliation asks into the base budget, including $9.4B for Golden Dome. Meanwhile, the UK, Germany and Norway announced new air-defence money for Ukraine after Russia struck two Kyiv bridges.

NATO

  • NATO launched STARLIFT at NATO EDGE 26 in İzmir to help allies get military satellites onto commercial rockets, including at short notice, through a network of Alliance and Korean spaceports. Belgium, Canada, Finland, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Türkiye, the UK and South Korea are funding it through NSPA. (NATO)
  • Breaking Defense notes that four original STARLIFT participants (France, Hungary, Luxembourg and the U.S.) are missing from the funding list. NATO gave no reason and disclosed no program cost. (Breaking Defense)
  • NATO and the U.S. Space Force also launched NATO's Global Data Marketplace to buy commercial space data, products and services, starting with space domain awareness. It runs on the Space Force's Joint Commercial Operations platform from Bluestaq. The first buy, for the Space Theatre Component at Ramstein, is expected by end-2026, and 222 companies from 17 allies have already joined. (NATO)
  • Opening EDGE 26, Deputy Secretary General Radmila Shekerinska called Russia the top long-term threat and said its hybrid campaign of sabotage, arson and drone incursions is intensifying. She said five allies are projected to hit 5% of GDP on defence this year, "nine years ahead of schedule." (UK Defence Journal)
  • At the 37th Ukraine Defence Contact Group at NATO HQ, the UK pledged £240M for more than 1,000 short-range air-defence missiles (Thales Belfast) and over a dozen radars, with deliveries from mid-December. The UK, Sweden and Ukraine also signed a letter of intent on Gripen fighters for Kyiv. (GOV.UK)
  • Germany will put $300M into NATO's PURL, jointly with Norway, to buy U.S. PAC-2/PAC-3 Patriot interceptors for Ukraine, plus radars, drones and F-16 ammunition. Pistorius also pressed Washington to allow licensed production of U.S. systems in Europe. (Kyiv Independent; Euronews)
  • Kyiv's NATO ambassador says Ukraine has never been this vulnerable to ballistic missiles. Allies are about €7B short of their €70B aid pledge for 2026, PURL faces a $1.9B shortfall on contracted deliveries, and Poland says it will stop new PURL funding after $100M. (POLITICO Europe)

European Union

  • EU defence ministers at the EDA Steering Board approved the 2026 CARD review, which endorses eight joint opportunities. They include cruise missiles, long-range interceptors, counter-UAS, and three "strategic enablers": space-based early warning and tracking, a secure defence cloud, and strategic airlift. Ministers also raised EDA's 2027 budget 8.7% to €78M. (European Defence Agency)
  • Europe's negotiating team for Ukraine is set: the E5, the Council and Commission, and NATO. Moscow says the wider format "has not been agreed" and may want more trilateral rounds first. European, U.S. and Ukrainian officials meet Thursday on the sidelines of the Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin, and Austria is circulating a draft EU mandate. (Euronews; Kyiv Independent)
  • Kaja Kallas is pushing for a role after being left off Europe's negotiating team. She says foreign ministers have drafted "maximum demands" for Russia, while Lithuania's minister complained the EU can't "speak with 27 microphones." (POLITICO Europe)
  • Defence Commissioner Kubilius says Brussels is exploring a defence-industry pact with Ukraine that would pair SAFE loans with the Ukraine support instrument for joint projects. Capitals have until Nov. 30 to bid for the remaining €21.3B in the second SAFE round. (2eu.brussels)
  • Rheinmetall told Naval News at Euronaval that it is pitching its 6,000-tonne, Aegis-equipped GMF 140 frigate to the U.S. Navy as a possible joint U.S.–European "NATO frigate," with 64 VLS cells and ballistic missile defence capability. (Naval News)

United States

  • Vulcan failure: ULA's first update says "low booster performance" just after liftoff caused early stage separation below orbital velocity. The Centaur upper stage and the solid boosters with the new nozzle fix performed normally, and the FAA is overseeing the investigation. Aviation Week notes that the BE-4 engines had been retrofitted after New Glenn's May pad explosion and burned about 30 seconds longer than planned. (ULA; Aviation Week)
  • With both Vulcan and New Glenn grounded, Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy are the only NSSL Lane 2 rockets flying. That deepens worries about a military launch bottleneck, especially since SpaceX plans to wind down Falcon around 2030. (Breaking Defense)
  • Space Systems Command awarded SpaceX, ULA and Blue Origin NSSL Phase 3 Lane 2 contract modifications with a combined ceiling of $985M, with work through April 2033. (Defense Daily)
  • Senate appropriators unveiled a ~$1.1T FY27 defense bill (vs. the $1.5T requested). It moves about $69B of reconciliation asks into discretionary funding: $9.4B for Golden Dome, $3B for the Defense Autonomous Warfare Group, $47.2B for munitions, and 25 extra F-35s. The continuing resolution expires Dec. 11. (Breaking Defense)
  • The Space Force is asking industry to help define a new cislunar spacecraft system targeting first launch in late 2029. Missions, payloads and orbits are still open. (SpaceNews)
  • SSC awarded about $10M in Phase 1 prototype deals to Anduril, Booz Allen Hamilton and Peerless for SEWOL, a cloud-based command system for the Space Force's counter-SATCOM electronic-warfare fleet. A 90-day bake-off will be followed by a down-select to one vendor. (SatNews)

European space

  • Thales Alenia Space signed with the Italian Space Agency to build a national L-band SAR satellite (2.2 t, 26 m² antenna). It continues SAOCOM-type L-band data and complements COSMO-SkyMed for security and civil-protection uses. (Thales Alenia Space)
  • Leonardo CEO Lorenzo Mariani says the Airbus–Thales–Leonardo "Bromo" space partners are finalising an antitrust remedies package for the Commission. He called the talks slow but "very constructive," while warning against structural remedies that would weaken the would-be European champion. (Borsa Italiana / Radiocor)
  • With Vulcan grounded, Ariane 6's next Amazon Leo mission (VA271/LE-04, 36 satellites on an Ariane 64) remains targeted for no earlier than Nov. 23 from Kourou. (Arianespace)
  • ESA signed contract amendments with Thales Alenia Space (with CNES support) moving the TeQuantS space quantum-communications project into a lab phase at CNES. The lab will test entangled-photon sources and satellite–ground timing for future secure quantum networks. (ESA)
  • EU Space Act: the European Parliament's ITRE committee vote is scheduled for Nov. 19, after the Irish Council presidency circulated a revised compromise. Trilogues could start in December. (Table.Briefings)

Global space & defense

  • Overnight, Russia fired ballistic, cruise and Zircon missiles plus 306 drones at Ukraine, killing 14 and damaging both of Kyiv's Northern and Southern bridges. About 700,000 households in Dnipropetrovsk lost power. (Kyiv Independent)
  • Xi, Trump and Putin are due to meet Thursday in Shenzhen on the APEC sidelines, the first such trilateral. Trump says denuclearisation, Iran, trade and Ukraine will come up, feeding Kyiv's "Yalta" fears. (The Guardian)
  • Iran's IRGC fired drones at a U.S. radar at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa base, its third strike on U.S. targets there in days, and Bahrain intercepted them. A tanker crew is missing after an attack in the Strait of Hormuz while Qatar and Oman mediate. (Al-Monitor / Reuters)
  • South Korea scrambled fighters after Russian military aircraft entered its air defence zone over the East Sea early Tuesday. They did not violate South Korean airspace. (CNA)
  • China launched its 27th batch of "satellite internet" LEO satellites (the state Guowang megaconstellation) on a Long March 12 from the Hainan commercial launch site. (GMT Eight)
